_meta.status: Documented vendor fees only — community anecdotes excluded from arithmetic. Sources verified 2026-06-12; see notes per provider.
_meta.fee_base_note: Paddle, Lemon Squeezy and Stripe Managed Payments all document that their percentage applies to the tax-inclusive charged total. Charge amounts in this analysis are treated as tax-inclusive totals accordingly.

xbc_assumption: XBC rate is an ASSUMPTION pending the published pricing plan: 2% of transaction value, percentage-only with NO minimum fee, on top of your own Stripe processing fees — XBC is not a merchant of record, so your existing Stripe fees still apply. One-line update here when pricing is final.

providers.name: Raw Stripe (DIY compliance)
notes: 2.9% + 30c US cards, +1.5% international, +0.7% Billing for subscriptions, +0.5% Stripe Tax calculation added when actual fees unavailable (https://stripe.com/pricing). NOTE: modeled rates are US pricing — EU/UK-domiciled accounts have different (typically lower) domestic card pricing; the actual-fees basis (live mode) is authoritative for your account.
EVERY registration and filing is on you — see the growth report for what that costs as thresholds get crossed.

providers.name: Paddle
notes: 5% + 50c on the TAX-INCLUSIVE total (https://www.paddle.com/pricing; fee base: https://www.paddle.com/help/manage/reporting/how-are-my-earnings-calculated).

Not modeled (undocumented): sales-currency to balance-currency FX spread; up-to-1.5% payout FX margin; $15 SWIFT payouts; $15 chargebacks. Community reports put international sellers at 7-8% effective.

Community-reported effective rate for international sellers: 7-8% — driven by an UNDOCUMENTED sales-to-balance currency FX spread that is NOT modeled even at range-high. Per-incident fees ($15 SWIFT payouts, $15 chargebacks) also excluded.

providers.name: Lemon Squeezy
notes: 5% + 50c tax-inclusive, +1.5% international, +0.5% subscriptions (https://docs.lemonsqueezy.com/help/getting-started/fees). PayPal +1.5% not modeled (share unknown).
Not modeled: 1% payout fee to non-US banks; $15 disputes. Stripe-owned; publicly migrating users toward Stripe Managed Payments.
Per-incident fees excluded: $15 disputes; PayPal payout 3% capped $30.

providers.name: Stripe Managed Payments
notes: 3.5% MoR fee on the tax-inclusive total IN ADDITION to standard processing (2.9% + 30c) (https://stripe.com/pricing#managed-payments; https://support.stripe.com/questions/managed-payments-pricing). +0.7% Billing for subscriptions.
Product constraints: digital products only; Checkout/Payment Links/mobile only — no Elements, no Connect, no third-party tax engines (https://docs.stripe.com/payments/managed-payments).

providers.name: XBC
notes: ASSUMPTION pending published pricing (see xbc_assumption): 2% of transaction value, percentage-only with no minimum fee, plus your own Stripe fees (modeled at US pricing when actual fees unavailable; EU/UK accounts have lower domestic pricing — live-mode actual fees are authoritative).
You keep your own Stripe account, customer relationships, payout schedule and exit path — see structure_facts.

polar_footnote: Polar.sh (developer-focused MoR on Stripe, $10M Accel seed): tiered 5%+50c free tier down to 3.4%+30c at $400/mo, +1.5% international, $15/dispute (https://polar.sh/docs/merchant-of-record/fees). Included as context, not a modeled column.

diy_compliance.note: PROTOTYPE sourced ranges per jurisdiction (registration agents/advisors vary widely; PRD open item #3 — needs sourcing review). Ranges, never point estimates.

merchant_of_record_tradeoffs: With an MoR, the MoR owns the merchant account and the customer payment relationship; switching later means migrating every saved payment method and active subscription.
MoR percentage fees are documented to apply to the tax-inclusive total — you pay fees on the tax you collect.
Payout timing and currency are on the MoR's schedule, not yours.
stripe_managed_payments_constraints: Digital products only; Checkout/Payment Links/mobile SDK only (no Elements/custom flows); no third-party tax engines; eligibility review required.
xbc_position: XBC is not an MoR: your Stripe account, your customers, your payouts. XBC handles tax calculation, invoicing, registrations and liability on cross-border sales.
Leaving XBC does not require migrating your payment stack.
diy_position: Cheapest on processing fees ONLY — every threshold crossing in the exposure report becomes a registration + periodic filings you own (see ranges in the growth report).

Non-resident registration in many jurisdictions effectively requires hiring a local tax agent or fiscal representative (e.g. South Korea, Japan, Switzerland) — that cost is what the DIY ranges estimate; 'cheapest fees' is not cheapest total.
compliance_burden: Running tax compliance yourself carries a documented time and money overhead the fee table doesn't show: the World Bank's Paying Taxes data puts the median business at ~268 hours per year on tax compliance (https://subnational.doingbusiness.org/en/data/exploretopics/paying-taxes).

Vertex estimates indirect-tax (VAT/GST) compliance costs run roughly 1–2% of turnover on top of the tax actually owed, and fall disproportionately on smaller businesses (https://www.vertexinc.com/resources/resource-library/quantifying-vat-compliance-costs).
doing_nothing: Not registering is not a zero-cost option. Once you cross a jurisdiction's threshold, uncollected VAT/GST/sales tax accrues as back taxes plus interest and penalties; the amounts are jurisdiction-specific and can exceed the tax originally due. The exposure report shows where you have already crossed.
